data.headline: TLT: distinguish lower long yields from overnight funding.
data.summary: November 2 long Treasury yields fell, providing a dated input directly relevant to duration analysis. Overnight secured funding then moved higher. Those are different parts of the rates market; neither observation supplies TLT total return, distribution adjustments or a measured release-day price response.

bull.text: The thirty-year Treasury yield declined from 5.31% to 5.28%, and the ten-year from 4.94% to 4.91%, between October 30 and November 2. Lower yields generally support existing fixed-rate bond values, all else equal; TLT performance was not measured.

bear.text: SOFR rose to 3.97% on November 3 from 3.95%. This overnight secured rate is not TLT’s long-duration yield and does not establish a change in the FOMC target or the Treasury term premium.

watch.text: Treasury bond futures asset managers were net long 383,981 contracts on October 27, while leveraged funds were net short 150,393. The earlier leveraged net short was 162,757; both gross longs and shorts rose, so this was not simply short covering.

limitations: Treasury yields describe November 2; SOFR and reverse-repo figures describe November 3. These are delayed official observations, not live prices or the market response to a release.
CFTC figures are October 27 futures-only category positions. Related futures differ from ETF shares and do not identify current purchases, fund flows or individual investors.
Current ETF prices, option chains, gamma, representative social sentiment and dark-pool direction remain independently unmeasured. Hosted displays are separate from saved evidence.
The interpretation describes possible transmission channels, not measured causation, a return prediction or a calibrated trading probability. No prospective model is qualified.
Treasury futures and TLT differ in instruments and duration. No verified total-return-adjusted price history or prospective outcome has been added.
